subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Internet Changes Everything
description: A quick win: understand The Internet Changes Everything.

hook.text: In 1995, only 16 million people used the internet. By 2000, it was 400 million.

buildup.text: The web created massive demand for servers. Every company needed a website, fast.

discovery.text: Hosting providers appeared, renting server space inside large data centers.

twist.text: But traffic was unpredictable. A viral moment could crash your entire site in seconds.

climax.text: Fixed server capacity couldn't handle a dynamic, unpredictable internet.

punchline.text: The web needed elastic computing. The cloud was the answer.

quiz.question: What fundamental problem did early web hosting face?
options: Fixed server capacity couldn't handle unpredictable traffic spikes
The internet was too slow for any business use
Hosting providers refused to serve commercial websites

details.summary: The commercialization of the internet in the 1990s created the infrastructure for cloud computing. TCP/IP standardized networking, the web browser made remote services accessible, and e-commerce proved that applications could run entirely over the network.
details.whyItMatters: Without the internet, cloud computing is impossible. The web transformed computing from an isolated activity to a connected service, enabling everything cloud providers offer today.
takeaways: TCP/IP standardized how computers communicate globally
Web browsers made remote applications accessible to everyone
E-commerce proved network-based applications could scale

faq.question: When did the internet become commercial?
faq.answer: The NSFNet backbone was decommissioned in 1995, completing the transition to commercial internet. The Mosaic browser launched in 1993, making the web visual and accessible. Amazon and eBay, both founded in the mid-1990s, proved e-commerce viability.

faq.question: What internet technologies enabled the cloud?
faq.answer: TCP/IP provided reliable network communication. HTTP and HTML enabled web applications. SSL/TLS secured online transactions. DNS provided naming infrastructure. Together, these technologies created the foundation for delivering computing as a remote service.
